working_title: Reading Deeper Re-Acquires the Attack: A Pre-Registered Read-Depth Robustness Trilemma for Deterministic Threat Verifiers
author: Daniel Gmys-Casiano (Skyframe Innovations)
framing_rationale: Conventional empirical shape — thesis, ladder, axes, pre-registered bands, measure all rungs (empty corner) — with the candidate-defense-then-refute device (v2_canonical → OOV → audit) living inside §§5–7 where it is most dramatic
evidence_base: Read-Depth Robustness Frontier, Phases A–E (Sessions S086–S090). No new measurement — written entirely from closed artifacts.
contribution_claims: The frontier + trilemma result: a pre-registered 5-rung read-depth robustness frontier; the good corner is empty under frozen bands (S088, SUPPORTED)

Adversarial refutation of the lone escape: a blind OOV LLM adversary defeats deterministic canonicalization on 2/4 malign string scenarios; named-IOC matching resists, structural/synonym matching falls; white-box ≈ black-box (S089, SUPPORTED_STRONG)

Independent-judge audit + reusable method: GPT-4o + Gemini with calibration controls corroborate the evasions are meaning-preserving threats, not lenient-judge artifacts (S090, ROBUST); the pre-registered frontier + LLM-proposes/code-disposes + independent audit recipe as a transferable methodological contribution

finding_1.one_line_claim: The good corner of the detection × framing-robustness frontier is empty: all rungs of the read-depth ladder cap at cumulative J=0.25 under pre-registered frozen bands

finding_2.one_line_claim: The lone apparent escape (v2_canonical) is defeated by a blind black-box OOV adversary on 2/4 malign scenarios; named-IOC scenarios resist in both arms

finding_3.one_line_claim: GPT-4o and Gemini independently corroborate 15/18 evading disguises are meaning-preserving threats; 4/4 calibration controls pass; audit verdict ROBUST

sections.title: Abstract
claims: Deterministic threat verifiers escape framing vulnerability by removing AI from the reading seat, but this forces shallow reading
A pre-registered 5-rung read-depth ladder reveals no rung simultaneously achieves high detection, framing-robustness, and data-integrity-cleanliness
The lone apparent escape is adversarially defeated by a blind out-of-vocabulary LLM adversary on 2/4 malign scenarios
Two independent judge families (GPT-4o, Gemini) corroborate the evasions are meaning-preserving threats under calibration controls
The trilemma is empirical and pre-registered, not a theoretical impossibility — but the good corner is empty as measured

sections.title: Introduction
claims: Deterministic verifiers were introduced to eliminate framing vulnerability in multi-agent LLM threat analysis, but determinism forces shallow reading
Deeper reading re-acquires either framing susceptibility or dependence on attacker-controlled structure — the central trilemma
Three contributions: pre-registered frontier (SUPPORTED), adversarial OOV refutation (SUPPORTED_STRONG), independent-judge audit (ROBUST)
Roadmap: §§2–3 background and ladder, §4 methodology, §§5–7 findings, §8 method contribution, §§9–11 discussion and limitations

sections.title: Background
claims: Adversarial framing injection in multi-agent LLM systems is documented: meaning-preserving rewording can flip agent verdicts without altering the underlying facts
Multi-agent LLM pipelines mix deterministic and LLM components; deterministic components buy stability at the cost of expressive reading depth
Robustness frontiers and pre-registration are underused in ML security evaluation; conflating framing-robustness with detection power obscures tradeoffs
OOV/evasion attacks on detectors show that pattern-matching rules with fixed vocabularies have a natural adversarial bypass via synonym substitution
Faithfulness of explanation surfaces in AI systems is distinct from decision stability — a recurring theme in XAI literature

sections.title: The ARES Verifier and the Read-Depth Ladder
claims: ARES is a three-agent deterministic threat analysis pipeline: Architect (LLM), Light Skeptic (deterministic rule engine), OracleJudge (deterministic); cite Papers 1–3 for full derivation

The Light Skeptic v2 ladder defines 5 read-depth rungs: v1_field (field presence only), v2_structured (high-threat field + stage logic), v2_lexical (exe-in-user-path regex), v2_canonical (canonicalize-then-match), llm_semantic (full LLM reading)
Each rung reads more of the evidence packet value content than the rung below it; deeper reading increases detection potential but re-introduces attacker-controlled surface
The DETERMINISTIC_TIERS registry and LADDER_ORDER in light_skeptic_v2_ladder.py are the code-reality anchor for the ladder definition

sections.title: Methodology: A Pre-Registered Frontier
claims: Adaptive Corpus C comprises 8 stratified scenarios: 4 malign string scenarios (M-lex × 2, M-syn × 1, M-patch × 1), 2 benign structural twins, 1 .com/.js carry-forward FP probe, 1 inject_authorization positive control

Three properties operationalized: P1 (detection) = Youden's J on malign vs benign; P2 (framing-robustness) = noise-gated majority-flip-rate under semantic operators; P3 (data-integrity) = encoded in cumulative J via FPR-inheritance from the structural tier
Two frontier views: standalone (each rung measured independently) and cumulative (each rung stacked on all prior); standalone reveals per-rung strength, cumulative reveals deployment reality
Frozen pre-registered bands: framing-robust iff X_sem ≤ 0.10; high detection iff cumulative J ≥ 0.50; good corner = both simultaneously
Decision rule locked before tier-4 run: SUPPORTED if good corner empty, FALSIFIED if any rung occupies it

sections.title: Finding 1: The Good Corner Is Empty
claims: S088 tier-4 live run (Sonnet 4, K=20, Corpus C digest 9401b7188ba790a5, $3.23): all four deterministic rungs cap at cumulative J=0.25 — the structural tier's FPR=0.75 propagates through the entire stack
Standalone view shows the genuine detection ladder: v1_field J=0.0, v2_structured J=0.25, v2_lexical J=0.50, v2_canonical J=0.75; the standalone-to-cumulative gap is P3's empirical signature
LLM tier (v2_semantic) shows standalone J=0.75, X_sem=0.125 [0.00, 0.38] — it detects but is framing-susceptible (RDF-M-SYN-001 suffix flip p=0.0005)
v2_canonical appears to occupy the good corner in standalone: J=0.75, X_sem=0.0 (framing-robust by construction) — this is the lone escape that §6 adversarially probes
Finding 1 SUPPORTED under the pre-registered bands: the cumulative view confirms the good corner is empty for all rungs

sections.title: Finding 2: The Lone Escape Is Adversarially Defeated
claims: OOV adversarial evasion protocol: 'LLM proposes, code disposes' — an LLM adversary generates disguises, a deterministic skeleton+novelty gate rejects invalid ones, an LLM judge confirms meaning-preservation
Black arm (blind, no source access) and white arm (with source access) run independently; K=8 candidates per scenario per arm; both arms ran on Sonnet, $0.106 total
v2_canonical evaded on RDF-M-LEX-002 (exe-in-temp) and RDF-M-SYN-001 (synonym-dropper) in both arms: adversarial X_scenario=0.50 in both arms
Named-IOC scenarios RDF-M-LEX-001 (lsass) and RDF-M-PATCH-001 (procdump) resist in both arms: zero flips; named-IOC matching cannot be disguised away while preserving threat meaning
White-box ≈ black-box: source access does not expand the evadable set; the evadable boundary tracks the attacker's ability to construct meaning-preserving synonyms, not knowledge of the vocabulary
OOV corpus digest a4ea1d0645152ffa; verdict SUPPORTED_STRONG — a blind adversary found holes in both evadable scenarios

sections.title: Finding 3: Independent-Judge Audit
claims: Leniency threat: Sonnet (the original judge) accepted all 64 disguise candidates with zero rejections — could the verdict SUPPORTED_STRONG be a judge-leniency artifact?

Independent audit panel: GPT-4o and Gemini re-judge all 18 evading disguises; 4 calibration controls (2 positive = evaded originals must read malign, 2 negative = benign twins must read benign) applied first
4/4 calibration controls pass: both independents correctly identify positive controls as malign and negative controls as benign — leniency hypothesis rejected at the calibration level
15/18 evading disguises: both-independents confirmed as meaning-preserving threats; 3/18 split (GPT-4o benign / Gemini+Sonnet malign) — splits cluster at the meaning-dilution boundary of SYN-001
Audit verdict ROBUST: the SUPPORTED_STRONG headline is not a lenient-judge artifact; GPT-4o is the stricter judge; total spend $0.0093

sections.title: The Method as a Contribution
claims: The three-layer recipe — pre-registered bands, LLM-proposes/code-disposes adversarial generation, independent-judge audit with calibration controls — is a transferable evaluation methodology
Pre-registration is what converts an empty corner from a curve-fit to a credible empirical result; the bands must be frozen before measurement, not fit after
LLM-proposes/code-disposes separates adversarial creativity (LLM) from adversarial validity (deterministic skeleton+novelty gate), preventing the adversary from exploiting the judge
The independent-judge audit with calibration controls is a reusable leniency-falsification instrument applicable to any LLM-judge-reliant evaluation

sections.title: Discussion
claims: The relocation thesis (Papers 1–3 + this paper): removing the AI from the reading seat does not remove the attack — it relocates it from framing-susceptibility to attacker-controlled-structure and then to adversarial OOV evasion

Not all deterministic rules are equally fragile: named-IOC matching (specific tool names like lsass/procdump) resists OOV evasion because you cannot disguise a specific tool name and still mean it; structural/synonym matching does not share this property
Production verifier design implication: the named-IOC class of rules may occupy a defensible corner of the trilemma; building a ladder anchored on IOC specificity is a candidate future direction

The honesty dividend of pre-registration: presenting a result where the pre-registered bands could have been falsified strengthens the credibility of the empty-corner claim beyond what post-hoc analysis could achieve

sections.title: Limitations
claims: Single corpus (Adaptive Corpus C); N=4 malign string scenarios — small; generalization to broader scenario distributions is untested
Single base-model family for the pipeline (Sonnet 4); cross-model generalization of the frontier result is untested
Single OOV adversary model (Sonnet); a second adversary family would strengthen the adversarial evasion claim
RDF-M-SYN-001 has no same-skeleton benign twin in Corpus C; its leniency control leans on the generic clean baseline (slightly weaker for the synonym class)
The 3-property claim is operationalized on a 2-axis frontier (P3 enters via the cumulative FPR cap, not a third independent axis)
Trilemma is an empirical, pre-registered frontier result on this setup — not a proven impossibility; a different ladder, corpus, or adversary might find a corner occupant

sections.title: Future Work
claims: Benign synonym-class twin for RDF-M-SYN-001 to close the leniency-control gap
Second and third OOV adversary families to assess adversary-model dependence of the evasion boundary
Larger Corpus C with more malign/benign scenario pairs across broader threat categories
Named-IOC + semantic reading as a candidate corner-occupant: a hybrid tier that anchors on IOC specificity before invoking LLM reading may escape the trilemma
